Title: OpenAI weighs fresh funding at $1.2 trillion valuation ahead of IPO | Artificial Intelligence News - Business Standard
Home / Technology / Artificial Intelligence / OpenAI weighs fresh funding at $1.2 trillion valuation ahead of IPO. # OpenAI weighs fresh funding at $1.2 trillion valuation ahead of IPO. ## Any decision to move forward with the fundraising effort will hinge on exactly when OpenAI decides to go public, a person familiar with the talks said. OpenAI is also considering legal restrictions about what information it may be able to share with private market investors ahead of an IPO | Image: Bloomberg. 2 min read Last Updated : Sep 16 2026 | 9:50 AMIST. OpenAI is holding early talks with investors about a fresh funding round that would value the ChatGPT creator at more than $1.2 trillion ahead of an initial public offering. Any decision to move forward with the fundraising effort will hinge on exactly when OpenAI decides to go public, a person familiar with the talks said, asking not to be identified. The talks were initiated by investors, the person said. OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman told Fortune earlier the company’s long-anticipated IPO is still in the works but would not happen this year. The additional funding, if the AI giant takes it, would provide flexibility to potentially push back its IPO further, by one or two quarters, another person familiar said. Another reason OpenAI could consider additional fundraising would be to support more mergers and acquisitions, the person said. A funding round of that magnitude may allow OpenAI to leapfrog its chief rival Anthropic, which raised funds in May at a $965 billion valuation, including the new investment. OpenAI is also considering legal restrictions about what information it may be able to share with private market investors ahead of an IPO, the person said. The Financial Times reported on the talks earlier on Tuesday, noting that the round would allow longtime backers to increase their exposure ahead of the company’s IPO. The Claude chatbot maker is seeking to raise as much as or more than SpaceX in an IPO that could take place as soon as October, Bloomberg has reported. ## Sam Altman urges caution on AI; Trump says US must keep its lead over China.

Title: Southport Acquisition II files for $200M IPO targeting AI
Bitcoin DeFi Ethereum NFTs AI Agents Regulation Web3 Business Ecosystem. Southport Acquisition II files for $200M IPO targeting AI. The blank-check company is betting big on artificial intelligence, following its predecessor's $230M raise in 2021. Southport Acquisition II, a freshly minted special purpose acquisition company, has filed for a $200 million initial public offering with one clear mission: find an AI company to take public. The SPAC hasn’t named a target yet, which is standard operating procedure for blank-check companies. This isn’t the Southport team’s first trip to the SPAC rodeo. The original Southport Acquisition Corp. completed a $230 million IPO back in December 2021. That predecessor entity has since pursued business combinations, including a shareholder vote on a deal with Angel Studios. Southport Acquisition II’s $200 million target is slightly smaller than its predecessor’s haul, but the strategic pivot toward AI represents a meaningful shift in thesis. Where the original SPAC cast a wider net, the sequel is laser-focused on artificial intelligence. No specific acquisition targets have been disclosed in the filing. No timeline for a potential business combination has been shared either. ### AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing. ## A crowded field of AI-hungry SPACs. Southport Acquisition II is far from alone in chasing AI through the SPAC structure. Berto Acquisition II, another blank-check entity, has upsized its own IPO to $274 million with a similar mandate focused on AI and related infrastructure. SPACs are, by design, a bet on management rather than a specific business. When you invest in Southport Acquisition II at IPO, you’re trusting the sponsors to find a compelling AI company, negotiate a fair valuation, and execute a merger that creates value for shareholders. The $200 million war chest gives Southport Acquisition II meaningful firepower, though many AI companies commanding the most attention from venture capitalists carry valuations well into the billions. That could push the SPAC toward earlier-stage or more niche AI businesses, or it could seek additional financing through PIPE deals to pursue larger targets. Title: The Business of AI: Understanding Funding Rounds and Valuation in Artificial Intelligence
# The Business of AI: Understanding Funding Rounds and Valuation in Artificial Intelligence. The Business of AI: Understanding Funding Rounds and Valuation in Artificial Intelligence. ## The Crucial Role of Valuation and Funding in AI's Ascent. Understanding how AI companies are valued and how they secure funding rounds is paramount for anyone looking to navigate or participate in this dynamic sector. This post will delve deep into the mechanics of AI funding rounds and the specific factors that influence valuation, offering practical insights into what makes an AI venture truly valuable in the eyes of the market and investors. The journey of an AI startup, much like any tech venture, typically involves a series of funding rounds, each serving a distinct purpose and attracting different types of investors. Valuation here is highly speculative, often based on the strength of the team, the novelty of the AI idea, and the perceived market potential rather than existing revenue or users. ### Series A: Proving Product-Market Fit. Once an AI company has a working MVP and demonstrates initial traction – perhaps with early users or pilot programs – it typically seeks **Series A funding**. For highly successful AI companies, late-stage funding may involve private equity firms or pre-IPO rounds, as they prepare for a potential public offering (IPO) or a major acquisition. ## The Nuances of AI Company Valuation: Beyond Traditional Metrics. AI's disruptive potential often means companies are valued not just on current revenue, but on their ability to capture a massive **Total Addressable Market (TAM)**. While revenue multiples eventually become important, early-stage AI companies might be valued more on user engagement, unique model adoption, or even the sheer computational power and efficiency of their AI. ## Challenges and Future Outlook in AI Valuation and Funding. Understanding **Valuation, Funding** in the AI sector is more than just comprehending financial terms; it's about grasping the intrinsic value of innovation, data, and human ingenuity. Unlike traditional AI systems that primarily analyze data or make predictions based on existing patterns, generative AI models create entirely new, original content.

Title: SpaceX pursues confidential IPO in March following xAI merger, aiming for a $1.75T valuation - Phoenix Strategy Group
# SpaceX pursues confidential IPO in March following xAI merger, aiming for a $1.75T valuation. SpaceX planning confidential IPO filing, eyeing a June listing and up to $1.75T–$2T valuation after xAI deal. Elon Musk’s space exploration giant, SpaceX, is reportedly preparing to take the next step toward going public with one of the most anticipated IPOs in history. Following its recent merger with Musk's artificial intelligence startup, xAI, the company is said to be targeting a staggering $1.75 trillion valuation. According to reports from Bloomberg, SpaceX plans to submit draft paperwork to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in March under a confidential filing. This strategic move would allow the company to review regulatory feedback and tweak its filing before making its financial details public. If the IPO proceeds as planned, the public listing could happen as early as June. At its projected $1.75 trillion valuation, the SpaceX offering would far surpass Saudi Aramco’s $29 billion debut in 2019, which currently holds the record for the largest IPO in history. ## xAI Merger and Valuation Surge. The company's proposed valuation follows its recent acquisition of xAI, Musk’s artificial intelligence venture. The merger reportedly valued the combined entity at $1.25 trillion earlier this month, setting the stage for what could become one of the largest tech IPOs ever undertaken. The company is also weighing the possibility of a dual-class share structure, a move that would give Musk and other key insiders enhanced voting control despite owning a smaller percentage of shares. Kalshi, a regulated U.S.-based prediction market, shows traders assigning a 47% chance that SpaceX will announce its IPO before June 1. Meanwhile, Polymarket, powered by blockchain technology, has traders betting on the company's potential to close its IPO at a valuation exceeding $2 trillion, with odds above 40%. ## A Pivotal Year for Tech IPOs. The possible SpaceX IPO would add to a broader wave of excitement in the tech sector, with reports indicating that other major players, such as OpenAI and Anthropic, may also explore going public. With its bold ambitions and the momentum from its xAI merger, SpaceX is poised to make history.

items.title: Dario Amodei — We Must Pace the Frontier
items.snippet: But like many technologies before it, AI brings risks, and because it is such a ...
items.raw_snippet: But like many technologies before it, AI brings risks, and because it is such a powerful technology, these risks are serious. I’ve written a lot about them too. They include the risk of losing control of AI systems, misuse of AI for cyberattacks and bioterrorism, and serious economic disruption. A race to the bottom, spurred by commercial incentives, can make these risks more acute. [...] Along with my co-founders and employees, I have grappled with this duality of risk and benefit since the beginning of Anthropic. Not building the technology deprives humanity of benefits or simply places AI in the hands of authoritarian powers, while building it too fast is reckless. We have sought a middle way: to show that it’s possible to build carefully and succeed commercially, and to make safety something on which AI companies compete. In other words, to create a race to the top. We have [...] his death, and I myself survived an early-stage cancer that would not have been treatable even fifty years ago. Carefully wielded, AI can be the latest in a long line of technological miracles that have uplifted and ennobled humanity.
